rules.title: Facts before spin
rules.statement: Material factual claims will be backed by identifiable public evidence.

detail.text: Opinions, estimates, interpretations and inferences will be identified as such. If the campaign publishes something materially wrong, the correction and original wording will remain publicly accessible.

rules.evidence: Source links, public corrections and the platform change log.

rules.title: Show the money
rules.statement: The campaign will cap individual contributions at $500 and publish campaign-finance information during the campaign.

items: The cap applies consistently to eligible monetary and in-kind contributions. Amounts that cannot be accepted will be returned or refunded and included in public reporting.

Published information will include contribution distribution, spending categories and material consultants, contractors, agencies, advisers, professional service providers and vendors receiving campaign funds.

rules.evidence: Contribution distribution, returned or refunded contributions, campaign spending, paid-relationship disclosures and the official filing.

rules.title: Donations buy no access
rules.statement: A donation will not purchase better access, a faster response, political preference, favourable treatment or advance access to decisions.

detail.text: The standard covers campaign responses and advocacy involving grants, contracts, procurement, planning, permitting, appointments and municipal services. Donors retain the same ordinary access as every other resident, no more and no less.

rules.evidence: Public corrections, breach disclosures and corrective action.

rules.title: Campaign in the open
rules.statement: Campaign communications will be attributable, factual and accountable.

detail.text: The campaign will not use fake community accounts, anonymous attack pages, concealed proxies or intermediaries to spread personal attacks, and it will not target candidates’ families or irrelevant private lives. Forceful, factual criticism of public records, statements, conduct, competence and policy remains fair game.

rules.evidence: Public campaign communications, corrections and breach disclosures.

rules.title: Protect people’s information
rules.statement: Taking part in the campaign will not be used to quietly build political profiles.

items: Poll choices will not be attached to campaign contact records, volunteer records, lawn-sign requests or political profiles.
Youth Idea Lab submissions remain private unless the campaign later receives permission to publish an idea.

Contact, volunteer, update, concern, media, conversation and lawn-sign records will be reviewed for deletion when no longer needed, subject to legal, security, dispute and election-compliance requirements.

Raw poll-vote and duplicate-prevention identifiers will be removed through campaign data maintenance after a poll has been closed for at least 180 days. Aggregate counts and public summaries may remain.

rules.evidence: Published privacy practices, corrections and disclosed failures.

rules.title: Change course in public
rules.statement: If the campaign changes a published position, the previous position, the reason for the change and the new position will remain publicly visible.

items: Campaign polls and consultations are inputs, not binding votes or scientific surveys.
After a poll or consultation, the campaign will report what it heard, where people disagreed and whether the result changed the campaign’s position.

If a poll, consultation or other credible evidence reveals a clear and substantial objection to a position, the campaign may change course, but it will explain the decision and preserve the earlier position rather than quietly editing it away.
Unmet commitments and corrective action will also remain publicly visible.

rules.evidence: Poll report-backs, corrections, the platform change log, disclosed failures and corrective action.

rules.title: Make, explain and own decisions
rules.statement: Town Hall exists to serve the people of Port Hope. I will make decisions, explain them, own the result and change course when the facts show that a better answer is needed.

items: The decision standard is: Listen, Test, Decide, Report back.
Relevant expertise, evidence, cost and public impact will be tested before a decision.
Formal mayoral powers will be used transparently and proportionately for a clear municipal purpose.

rules.title: No Wrong Door
rules.statement: Residents should not need to know whether the Town, County, Province, police, public health, a utility or another body controls an issue before asking Town Hall for help.

items: Town Hall will explain responsibility, provide a useful next step, help navigate the system, advocate or escalate where appropriate and carry the file until there is a clear answer.
Technology should make Town Hall easier to deal with by reducing repetitive work, improving follow-up and making information easier to find while preserving human judgement and privacy.

rules.title: Decide in public. Show the work.
rules.statement: Major municipal decisions should be debated and decided in public. Closed sessions should be used only where the law permits and a compelling public-interest reason makes confidentiality necessary.

items: Before a major vote, residents should be able to see the problem, options, cost and funding source, responsibility, timeline, risks, consequences of doing nothing, who benefits, who pays and the impacts on both wards.
When confidentiality is necessary, Town Hall should publish as much as legally possible about the subject, the reason confidentiality was required and the eventual decision.

rules.title: Test small before buying big
rules.statement: Port Hope should test new methods in ways that protect taxpayers and produce evidence residents can inspect.

detail.text: Small pilots should begin with clear outcomes, fixed limits, independent evaluation and published results. A successful pilot should still proceed through lawful procurement before a major rollout.

rules.title: Listen beyond the loudest room
rules.statement: Organized groups will be heard, but no group will be treated as representative of the whole community simply because it is louder, more organized or more present at meetings.

items: Decisions will weigh representative public opinion, directly affected residents, expert evidence, lived experience, legal rights, costs and the long-term public interest.
A small organized minority will not automatically override a clear and credible majority view. A majority will not override legal rights, evidence or the municipality’s duties.
Council will make, explain and own the final decision.

rules.title: One Port Hope
rules.statement: Port Hope is one municipality, but equal treatment does not always require identical delivery.

detail.text: Major decisions will account for the different needs of Ward 1 and Ward 2, including roads, agriculture, emergency access, servicing, infrastructure, downtown pressures, who benefits and who pays.
